newsitem.title: USA: Agents find it easier to protect Clinton than shoes.
newsitem.headline: Agents find it easier to protect Clinton than shoes.

text.p: Protecting President Clinton is one thing. But a trio of Secret Service agents has learned that keeping possession of your shoes on a Florida beach can be even more difficult.

Three agents who accompanied Clinton on a campaign swing through Florida last week were the victims of theft while taking a quick dip in the ocean. The three men lost their Secret Service badges, cash, travelers checks, credit cards, jewelry -- even shoes and socks, according to a police report.

The agents hit the beach in mid-afternoon on October 23, about an hour after Clinton left Daytona Beach aboard Air Force One. Like many naive Florida tourists, the agents left their belongings tucked into shoes and socks while they frolicked in the surf.
Minutes later the items were gone, and some thief, still on the loose on Wednesday, probably wondered just how much trouble you can get into for stealing Secret Service badges.

Also missing were hotel keys, $110 in cash, six credit cards, automatic teller cards, $500 in travelers checks, a pair of $120 sun glasses and two watches worth $190. The badges and empty wallets turned up several hours later when a man told police he had found them near a biker bar.
The Secret Service, which apparently takes its name seriously, tried to keep the embarrassing incident under wraps by ordering the city's Beach Department not to release the incident report.
Florida law, however, makes such documents public. Officials released the report late on Tuesday with the agents' names blacked out.
